name: Srinagar–Kanyakumari Highway
aka: Formed from the former NH 1A, NH 1, NH 2, NH 3, NH 75, NH 26 and NH 7

timeline.event: Created in the national highway renumbering by merging seven older highways
Chenani–Nashri tunnel (9.28 km), India's longest road tunnel at the time, opens on the Jammu–Srinagar section

history: NH 44 is India's longest national highway, running the entire length of the country from Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari at the southern tip. It was created in 2010 by joining seven older highways into one continuous route, and it forms the backbone of the North–South Corridor project. Along the way it crosses the Himalayas, the Gangetic plains, the Deccan plateau and the southern coastal plains.
facts: India's longest national highway at about 3,745 km.
Passes through 11 states and union territories.
The Jammu–Srinagar section includes the 9.28 km Chenani–Nashri (Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee) tunnel.
Old highway numbers merged into it include the famous NH 7 (Nagpur–Kanyakumari).
Part of the Delhi–Ambala stretch follows the historic Grand Trunk Road.
significance: NH 44 is the spine of India's road network — the one highway that ties the Kashmir valley, the northern plains, central India and the deep south into a single route. Lakhs of trucks use it to move farm produce, factory goods and fuel between north and south every day, and for Jammu & Kashmir it is the main all-weather lifeline to the rest of the country.

engineering.name: Chenani–Nashri (Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee) Tunnel
engineering.note: 9.28 km — India's longest road tunnel when it opened in 2017, bypassing avalanche-prone hairpins

engineering.name: Qazigund–Banihal Tunnel
engineering.note: 8.45 km twin-tube tunnel under the Pir Panjal range, opened 2021, keeps the Srinagar road open in winter

engineering.name: Panipat elevated expressway
engineering.note: a long elevated stretch carries through-traffic clear over Panipat city

interchanges.name: Agra
interchanges.note: NH 19 splits off here toward Kanpur and Kolkata (the Golden Quadrilateral east arm)

interchanges.name: Nagpur
interchanges.note: crosses NH 53 at the geographic centre of India — the Zero Mile marker city

interchanges.name: Bengaluru
interchanges.note: meets NH 48 and NH 75 on the city's ring

travelNotes: Driving the full length is a 3,700 km, multi-day road trip — most people do it in four to five days. The Delhi–Agra and Bengaluru–Salem stretches are the busiest; dense winter fog slows the Punjab–Haryana section in December–January, and the Jammu–Srinagar mountain leg can close for hours after heavy snow or landslides, so check conditions before that stretch.
futureUpgrades: Remaining 4-lane sections are being widened to 6 lanes in phases.
The Delhi–Amritsar–Katra Expressway will take over much of the long-distance traffic toward Jammu once complete.
